verdict.rationale: LangGraph's core is an open-source framework installed with pip and run in your own environment. The official LangGraph CLI also builds and runs the Agent Server locally, with all run/thread/assistant endpoints and a managed database for checkpointing, and you can plug in your own Postgres checkpointer. However, the evidence only documents local runs; production self-hosting of the server is not documented, and a community member asks how to deploy beyond running `langgraph serve` locally. missing for 10: documented production self-hosted deployment of the Agent Server, explicit open-source license terms, independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: LangGraph CLI is a command-line tool for building and running the Agent Server locally. The resulting server exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc., and includes supporting services such as a managed database for checkpointing and storage.
In production, use a checkpointer backed by a database: from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres import PostgresSaver
LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents.
